sarvadvārāṇi saṃyamya mano hṛdi nirudhya ca mūrdhnyādhāyātmanaḥ prāṇamāsthito yogadhāraṇām 8-12
...uttering the single syllable Om, which is Brahman, and remembering me, whoever departs, leaving the body, reaches the supreme goal.
omityekākṣaraṃ brahma vyāharanmāmanusmaran yaḥ prayāti tyajandehaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim 8-13
Partha, for the yogi who remembers me constantly, day after day, with a mind turned to nothing else, ever united — for him I am easy to reach.
ananyacetāḥ satataṃ yo māṃ smarati nityaśaḥ tasyāhaṃ sulabhaḥ pārtha nityayuktasya yoginaḥ 8-14
Having come to me, these great souls, who have reached the highest perfection, do not return to rebirth, that impermanent home of sorrow.
māmupetya punarjanma duḥkhālayamaśāśvatam nāpnuvanti mahātmānaḥ saṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ gatāḥ 8-15
Arjuna, all worlds, up to the realm of Brahma, are subject to return; but having come to me, son of Kunti, there is no further birth.
ābrahmabhuvanāllokāḥ punarāvartino'rjuna māmupetya tu kaunteya punarjanma na vidyate 8-16
Those who know that a day of Brahma lasts a thousand ages, and that his night likewise ends after a thousand ages, truly understand day and night.
sahasrayugaparyantamaharyadbrahmaṇo viduḥ rātriṃ yugasahasrāntāṃ te'horātravido janāḥ 8-17
At the coming of that day, all manifest things emerge from the unmanifest; at the coming of night they dissolve back into that very thing called the unmanifest.
avyaktādvyaktayaḥ sarvāḥ prabhavantyaharāgame rātryāgame pralīyante tatraivāvyaktasaṃjñake 8-18
This same multitude of beings, coming into existence again and again, dissolves helplessly when night falls, Partha, and springs forth again when day dawns.
bhūtagrāmaḥ sa evāyaṃ bhūtvā bhūtvā pralīyate rātryāgame'vaśaḥ pārtha prabhavatyaharāgame 8-19
But beyond that unmanifest there is another unmanifest, eternal existence, which does not perish when all beings perish.
parastasmāttu bhāvo'nyo'vyakto'vyaktātsanātanaḥ yaḥ sa sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati 8-20
This unmanifest is called the imperishable, and it is said to be the supreme goal. Those who reach it do not return; that is my highest abode.
avyakto'kṣara ityuktastamāhuḥ paramāṃ gatim yaṃ prāpya na nivartante taddhāma paramaṃ mama 8-21
That supreme Person, Partha, within whom all beings dwell and by whom all this is pervaded, can be reached through undivided devotion.
puruṣaḥ sa paraḥ pārtha bhaktyā labhyastvananyayā yasyāntaḥsthāni bhūtāni yena sarvamidaṃ tatam 8-22
Now, best of the Bharatas, I will tell you the times at which yogis who depart either do not return or do return.
yatra kāle tvanāvṛttimāvṛttiṃ caiva yoginaḥ prayātā yānti taṃ kālaṃ vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha 8-23
Fire, light, day, the bright half of the month, the six months of the sun's northern course — departing by this path, those who know Brahman go to Brahman.
agnirjyotirahaḥ śuklaḥ ṣaṇmāsā uttarāyaṇam tatra prayātā gacchanti brahma brahmavido janāḥ 8-24
Smoke, night, the dark half of the month, the six months of the sun's southern course — taking this path, the yogi reaches the light of the moon and returns.
dhūmo rātristathā kṛṣṇaḥ ṣaṇmāsā dakṣiṇāyanam tatra cāndramasaṃ jyotiryogī prāpya nivartate 8-25
These two paths of the world, the bright and the dark, are held to be eternal. By one a person goes and does not return; by the other he comes back again.
śuklakṛṣṇe gatī hyete jagataḥ śāśvate mate ekayā yātyanāvṛttimanyayāvartate punaḥ 8-26
Knowing these two paths, Partha, no yogi is ever misled. Therefore, Arjuna, be steadfast in yoga at all times.
naite sṛtī pārtha jānanyogī muhyati kaścana tasmātsarveṣu kāleṣu yogayukto bhavārjuna 8-27
Whatever reward of merit is promised for study of the Vedas, for sacrifices, austerities and gifts — the yogi who knows this goes beyond all of it and reaches the supreme, primal abode.
vedeṣu yajñeṣu tapaḥsu caiva dāneṣu yat puṇyaphalaṃ pradiṣṭam atyeti tatsarvamidaṃ viditvā yogī paraṃ sthānamupaiti cādyam 8-28
Because you do not find fault, I will now tell you the most hidden knowledge of all, together with its practical realisation; once you know it, you will be set free from what is harmful.
idaṃ tu te guhyatamaṃ pravakṣyāmyanasūyave jñānaṃ vijñānasahitaṃ yajjñātvā mokṣyase'śubhāt 9-1

This is the king of all knowledge and the king of all secrets, supremely purifying. It can be known by direct experience, it is in keeping with dharma, it is very easy to practise, and it never perishes.
rājavidyā rājaguhyaṃ pavitramidamuttamam pratyakṣāvagamaṃ dharmyaṃ susukhaṃ kartumavyayam 9-2
People who have no faith in this teaching, Parantapa, do not reach me; they turn back onto the road of death and rebirth.
aśraddadhānāḥ puruṣā dharmasyāsya parantapa aprāpya māṃ nivartante mṛtyusaṃsāravartmani 9-3
This whole universe is pervaded by me in my unmanifest form. All beings rest in me, but I do not rest in them.
mayā tatamidaṃ sarvaṃ jagadavyaktamūrtinā matsthāni sarvabhūtāni na cāhaṃ teṣvavasthitaḥ 9-4
And yet beings do not rest in me either: see my divine power. My Self sustains all beings and brings them into existence, yet it does not dwell in them.
na ca matsthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogamaiśvaram bhūtabhṛnna ca bhūtastho mamātmā bhūtabhāvanaḥ 9-5
Just as the great wind, moving everywhere, always remains within space, understand that in the same way all beings remain within me.
yathākāśasthito nityaṃ vāyuḥ sarvatrago mahān tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni matsthānītyupadhāraya 9-6
At the end of a cosmic age, Kaunteya, all beings pass back into my own nature; at the start of the next age I send them forth again.
sarvabhūtāni kaunteya prakṛtiṃ yānti māmikām kalpakṣaye punastāni kalpādau visṛjāmyaham 9-7
Taking hold of my own nature, I send forth again and again this whole multitude of beings, which is helpless under the sway of nature.
prakṛtiṃ svāmavaṣṭabhya visṛjāmi punaḥ punaḥ bhūtagrāmamimaṃ kṛtsnamavaśaṃ prakṛtervaśāt 9-8
Those actions do not bind me, Dhananjaya, for I sit among them as one who is indifferent, unattached to those deeds.
na ca māṃ tāni karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanaṃjaya udāsīnavadāsīnamasaktaṃ teṣu karmasu 9-9
With me as overseer, nature gives birth to all that moves and all that is still; for this reason, Kaunteya, the world keeps turning.
mayādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sacarācaram hetunānena kaunteya jagadviparivartate 9-10
Deluded people look down on me when I take on a human body, not knowing my higher nature as the great Lord of all beings.
avajānanti māṃ mūḍhā mānuṣīṃ tanumāśritam paraṃ bhāvamajānanto mama bhūtamaheśvaram 9-11
Their hopes are empty, their actions futile and their knowledge useless; senseless, they cling to the deluding nature of fiends and demons.
moghāśā moghakarmāṇo moghajñānā vicetasaḥ rākṣasīmāsurīṃ caiva prakṛtiṃ mohinīṃ śritāḥ 9-12
But great souls, Partha, who take refuge in the divine nature, worship me with minds turned to nothing else, knowing me as the imperishable source of all beings.
mahātmānastu māṃ pārtha daivīṃ prakṛtimāśritāḥ bhajantyananyamanaso jñātvā bhūtādimavyayam 9-13
Always singing my glory, striving with firm resolve, and bowing to me in devotion, they worship me ever united with me.
satataṃ kīrtayanto māṃ yatantaśca dṛḍhavratāḥ namasyantaśca māṃ bhaktyā nityayuktā upāsate 9-14
Others worship me by offering the sacrifice of knowledge, seeing me as one, as distinct, and in many ways as the one whose faces are everywhere.
jñānayajñena cāpyanye yajanto māmupāsate ekatvena pṛthaktvena bahudhā viśvatomukham 9-15
I am the ritual and I am the sacrifice; I am the offering to the ancestors and the healing herb; I am the sacred chant, I am the clarified butter, I am the fire and I am the act of offering.
ahaṃ kraturahaṃ yajñaḥ svadhāhamahamauṣadham mantro'hamahamevājyamahamagnirahaṃ hutam 9-16
I am the father of this world, its mother, its upholder and its grandsire. I am what is to be known, the purifier, the syllable Om, and the Rig, Sama and Yajur Vedas as well.
pitāhamasya jagato mātā dhātā pitāmahaḥ vedyaṃ pavitramoṃkāra ṛksāma yajureva ca 9-17
I am the goal, the sustainer, the master and the witness; the home, the refuge and the friend; the origin and the dissolution, the ground, the storehouse and the seed that never decays.
gatirbhartā prabhuḥ sākṣī nivāsaḥ śaraṇaṃ suhṛt prabhavaḥ pralayaḥ sthānaṃ nidhānaṃ bījamavyayam 9-18
I give heat; I hold back the rain and send it down. I am immortality and death as well, being and non-being, Arjuna.
tapāmyahamahaṃ varṣaṃ nigṛhṇāmyutsṛjāmi ca amṛtaṃ caiva mṛtyuśca sadasaccāhamarjuna 9-19

Those versed in the three Vedas, who drink the soma and are cleansed of sin, worship me through sacrifices and pray for a path to heaven. Reaching the holy world of the king of the gods through their merit, they enjoy the divine pleasures of the gods in heaven.
traividyā māṃ somapāḥ pūtapāpā yajñairiṣṭvā svargatiṃ prārthayante te puṇyamāsādya surendraloka- maśnanti divyāndivi devabhogān 9-20

Having enjoyed that vast heavenly world, they return to the world of mortals once their merit is spent. In this way, following the ritual dharma of the three Vedas and craving pleasures, they keep going and coming.
te taṃ bhuktvā svargalokaṃ viśālaṃ kṣīṇe puṇye martyalokaṃ viśanti evaṃ trayīdharmamanuprapannā gatāgataṃ kāmakāmā labhante 9-21
But those who think of me alone and worship me with no other thought, ever devoted to me: I myself take on their welfare, bringing them what they need and keeping safe what they have.
ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham 9-22
Even those who are devoted to other gods and worship them with faith, Kaunteya, are in fact worshipping me alone, though not in the proper way.
ye'pyanyadevatābhaktā yajante śraddhayānvitāḥ te'pi māmeva kaunteya yajantyavidhipūrvakam 9-23
For I am the enjoyer and the lord of every sacrifice. But they do not know me as I truly am, and so they fall back.
ahaṃ hi sarvayajñānāṃ bhoktā ca prabhureva ca na tu māmabhijānanti tattvenātaścyavanti te 9-24
Those devoted to the gods go to the gods, those devoted to the ancestors go to the ancestors, those who worship spirits go to the spirits, and those who worship me come to me.
yānti devavratā devānpitṝnyānti pitṛvratāḥ bhūtāni yānti bhūtejyā yānti madyājino'pi mām 9-25
Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or some water, that offering of love from a pure-hearted person I accept.
patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati tadahaṃ bhaktyupahṛtamaśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ 9-26
Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer in the fire, whatever you give and whatever discipline you practise, Kaunteya, do it as an offering to me.
yatkaroṣi yadaśnāsi yajjuhoṣi dadāsi yat yattapasyasi kaunteya tatkuruṣva madarpaṇam 9-27
In this way you will be freed from the bonds of action and their good and bad results. With your mind set firm in the yoga of renunciation, you will be liberated and come to me.
śubhāśubhaphalairevaṃ mokṣyase karmabandhanaiḥ saṃnyāsayogayuktātmā vimukto māmupaiṣyasi 9-28
I am the same toward all beings; no one is hateful to me and no one is my favourite. But those who worship me with devotion are in me, and I am in them.
samo'haṃ sarvabhūteṣu na me dveṣyo'sti na priyaḥ ye bhajanti tu māṃ bhaktyā mayi te teṣu cāpyaham 9-29
Even if a person of very bad conduct worships me with undivided devotion, he should be regarded as good, for he has made the right resolve.
api cetsudurācāro bhajate māmananyabhāk sādhureva sa mantavyaḥ samyagvyavasito hi saḥ 9-30
He quickly becomes righteous and attains lasting peace. Declare it boldly, Kaunteya: my devotee never perishes.
kṣipraṃ bhavati dharmātmā śaśvacchāntiṃ nigacchati kaunteya pratijānīhi na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati 9-31
For, Partha, those who take refuge in me, even those of lowly birth, women, Vaishyas and Shudras too, reach the highest goal.
māṃ hi pārtha vyapāśritya ye'pi syuḥ pāpayonayaḥ striyo vaiśyāstathā śūdrāste'pi yānti parāṃ gatim 9-32
How much more so, then, pure Brahmins and devoted royal sages! Having come into this passing and joyless world, worship me.
kiṃ punarbrāhmaṇāḥ puṇyā bhaktā rājarṣayastathā anityamasukhaṃ lokamimaṃ prāpya bhajasva mām 9-33
Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, offer worship to me and bow down to me. Joining yourself to me in this way, with me as your highest aim, you will come to me.
manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru māmevaiṣyasi yuktvaivamātmānaṃ matparāyaṇaḥ 9-34
Listen once more, mighty-armed one, to my supreme word, which I will speak to you because you delight in it and because I wish you well.
bhūya eva mahābāho śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ yatte'haṃ prīyamāṇāya vakṣyāmi hitakāmyayā 10-1
Neither the hosts of gods nor the great sages know my origin, for I am the source of the gods and of the great sages in every way.
na me viduḥ suragaṇāḥ prabhavaṃ na maharṣayaḥ ahamādirhi devānāṃ maharṣīṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ 10-2
Whoever knows me as unborn and without beginning, the great Lord of the worlds, is free of delusion among mortals and is released from all sins.
yo māmajamanādiṃ ca vetti lokamaheśvaram asaṃmūḍhaḥ sa martyeṣu sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate 10-3
Understanding, knowledge, freedom from confusion, patience, truthfulness, self-control and calm; pleasure and pain, coming into being and ceasing to be, fear and fearlessness;
buddhirjñānamasaṃmohaḥ kṣamā satyaṃ damaḥ śamaḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhavo'bhāvo bhayaṃ cābhayameva ca 10-4
non-violence, evenness, contentment, austerity, generosity, fame and disgrace: all these varied states of beings arise from me alone.
ahiṃsā samatā tuṣṭistapo dānaṃ yaśo'yaśaḥ bhavanti bhāvā bhūtānāṃ matta eva pṛthagvidhāḥ 10-5
The seven great sages of old and the four Manus too were born of my mind and share my nature; from them came all the creatures of this world.
maharṣayaḥ sapta pūrve catvāro manavastathā madbhāvā mānasā jātā yeṣāṃ loka imāḥ prajāḥ 10-6
Whoever truly knows this splendour and power of mine is joined to me by unwavering yoga; of this there is no doubt.
etāṃ vibhūtiṃ yogaṃ ca mama yo vetti tattvataḥ so'vikampena yogena yujyate nātra saṃśayaḥ 10-7
I am the origin of everything, and from me everything proceeds. Knowing this, the wise worship me, filled with love.
ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṃ pravartate iti matvā bhajante māṃ budhā bhāvasamanvitāḥ 10-8
With their minds on me and their lives given to me, enlightening one another and always speaking of me, they are content and full of joy.
maccittā madgataprāṇā bodhayantaḥ parasparam kathayantaśca māṃ nityaṃ tuṣyanti ca ramanti ca 10-9
To those who are always devoted and worship me with love, I give the yoga of understanding by which they come to me.
teṣāṃ satatayuktānāṃ bhajatāṃ prītipūrvakam dadāmi buddhiyogaṃ taṃ yena māmupayānti te 10-10
Out of compassion for them alone, dwelling in their hearts, I destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge.
teṣāmevānukampārthamahamajñānajaṃ tamaḥ nāśayāmyātmabhāvastho jñānadīpena bhāsvatā 10-11
You are the supreme Brahman, the supreme abode, the supreme purifier: the eternal, divine Person, the first of the gods, unborn and all-pervading.
arjuna uvāca paraṃ brahma paraṃ dhāma pavitraṃ paramaṃ bhavān puruṣaṃ śāśvataṃ divyamādidevamajaṃ vibhum 10-12
So all the sages describe you, and so do the divine sage Narada, Asita, Devala and Vyasa; and now you yourself are telling me.
āhustvāmṛṣayaḥ sarve devarṣirnāradastathā asito devalo vyāsaḥ svayaṃ caiva bravīṣi me 10-13
All that you tell me, Keshava, I accept as true. Indeed, Lord, neither the gods nor the demons understand your manifestation.
sarvametadṛtaṃ manye yanmāṃ vadasi keśava na hi te bhagavanvyaktiṃ vidurdevā na dānavāḥ 10-14
Only you know yourself through yourself, Supreme Person, source of beings, lord of beings, god of gods, master of the world.
svayamevātmanātmānaṃ vettha tvaṃ puruṣottama bhūtabhāvana bhūteśa devadeva jagatpate 10-15
Please tell me fully of your divine glories, the manifestations through which you pervade these worlds and abide in them.
vaktumarhasyaśeṣeṇa divyā hyātmavibhūtayaḥ yābhirvibhūtibhirlokānimāṃstvaṃ vyāpya tiṣṭhasi 10-16
How am I to know you, Yogi, while constantly meditating on you? In which of your many forms, Lord, should I think of you?
kathaṃ vidyāmahaṃ yogiṃstvāṃ sadā paricintayan keṣu keṣu ca bhāveṣu cintyo'si bhagavanmayā 10-17
Tell me again in detail, Janardana, of your power and your glories, for I never tire of hearing your nectar-like words.
vistareṇātmano yogaṃ vibhūtiṃ ca janārdana bhūyaḥ kathaya tṛptirhi śṛṇvato nāsti me'mṛtam 10-18
Very well, best of the Kurus, I will tell you of my divine glories, but only the chief ones, for there is no end to my extent.
hanta te kathayiṣyāmi divyā hyātmavibhūtayaḥ prādhānyataḥ kuruśreṣṭha nāstyanto vistarasya me 10-19
I am the Self, Gudakesha, seated in the heart of every being. I am the beginning, the middle and the end of all beings.
ahamātmā guḍākeśa sarvabhūtāśayasthitaḥ ahamādiśca madhyaṃ ca bhūtānāmanta eva ca 10-20
Among the Adityas I am Vishnu; among lights, the radiant sun; among the Maruts I am Marichi; and among the stars, the moon.
ādityānāmahaṃ viṣṇurjyotiṣāṃ raviraṃśumān marīcirmarutāmasmi nakṣatrāṇāmahaṃ śaśī 10-21
Among the Vedas I am the Sama Veda; among the gods I am Indra; among the senses I am the mind; and in living beings I am consciousness.
vedānāṃ sāmavedo'smi devānāmasmi vāsavaḥ indriyāṇāṃ manaścāsmi bhūtānāmasmi cetanā 10-22
Among the Rudras I am Shankara; among the Yakshas and Rakshasas, Kubera, lord of wealth; among the Vasus I am fire; and among mountain peaks, Meru.
rudrāṇāṃ śaṃkaraścāsmi vitteśo yakṣarakṣasām vasūnāṃ pāvakaścāsmi meruḥ śikhariṇāmaham 10-23
Know me, Partha, as Brihaspati, chief of household priests. Among army commanders I am Skanda, and among bodies of water, the ocean.
purodhasāṃ ca mukhyaṃ māṃ viddhi pārtha bṛhaspatim senānīnāmahaṃ skandaḥ sarasāmasmi sāgaraḥ 10-24
Among the great sages I am Bhrigu; among utterances, the single syllable Om. Among sacrifices I am the sacrifice of silent repetition, and among things that stand firm, the Himalaya.
maharṣīṇāṃ bhṛgurahaṃ girāmasmyekamakṣaram yajñānāṃ japayajño'smi sthāvarāṇāṃ himālayaḥ 10-25
Among all trees I am the sacred fig; among the divine sages, Narada; among the Gandharvas, Chitraratha; and among the perfected ones, the sage Kapila.
aśvatthaḥ sarvavṛkṣāṇāṃ devarṣīṇāṃ ca nāradaḥ gandharvāṇāṃ citrarathaḥ siddhānāṃ kapilo muniḥ 10-26
Among horses know me as Uchchaihshravas, born of the churning for nectar; among lordly elephants, Airavata; and among men, the king.
uccaiḥśravasamaśvānāṃ viddhi māmamṛtodbhavam airāvataṃ gajendrāṇāṃ narāṇāṃ ca narādhipam 10-27
Among weapons I am the thunderbolt; among cows, the wish-fulfilling Kamadhenu. I am Kandarpa, the god of love, who brings forth offspring, and among serpents I am Vasuki.
āyudhānāmahaṃ vajraṃ dhenūnāmasmi kāmadhuk prajanaścāsmi kandarpaḥ sarpāṇāmasmi vāsukiḥ 10-28
Among the Nagas I am Ananta; among the beings of the waters, Varuna; among the ancestors, Aryaman; and among those who restrain, I am Yama.
anantaścāsmi nāgānāṃ varuṇo yādasāmaham pitṝṇāmaryamā cāsmi yamaḥ saṃyamatāmaham 10-29
Among the Daityas I am Prahlada; among those who count, I am Time; among beasts, the lion; and among birds, Garuda, son of Vinata.
prahlādaścāsmi daityānāṃ kālaḥ kalayatāmaham mṛgāṇāṃ ca mṛgendro'haṃ vainateyaśca pakṣiṇām 10-30
Among purifiers I am the wind; among those who bear weapons, Rama; among sea creatures, the makara; and among rivers, the Ganga.
pavanaḥ pavatāmasmi rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāmaham jhaṣāṇāṃ makaraścāsmi srotasāmasmi jāhnavī 10-31
Of all creations I am the beginning, the end and the middle too, Arjuna. Among kinds of knowledge I am knowledge of the Self, and in those who debate, I am the reasoning that seeks truth.
sargāṇāmādirantaśca madhyaṃ caivāhamarjuna adhyātmavidyā vidyānāṃ vādaḥ pravadatāmaham 10-32
Among letters I am the letter A, and among compounds, the copulative compound. I alone am unending Time, and I am the sustainer whose face is turned everywhere.
akṣarāṇāmakāro'smi dvandvaḥ sāmāsikasya ca ahamevākṣayaḥ kālo dhātāhaṃ viśvatomukhaḥ 10-33
I am death that carries off everything, and the birth of all that is yet to be. Among feminine qualities I am fame, prosperity, speech, memory, intelligence, steadfastness and forbearance.
mṛtyuḥ sarvaharaścāhamudbhavaśca bhaviṣyatām kīrtiḥ śrīrvākca nārīṇāṃ smṛtirmedhā dhṛtiḥ kṣamā 10-34
Among Sama hymns I am the Brihat Saman; among metres, the Gayatri; among months, Margashirsha; and among seasons, flower-bearing spring.
bṛhatsāma tathā sāmnāṃ gāyatrī chandasāmaham māsānāṃ mārgaśīrṣo'hamṛtūnāṃ kusumākaraḥ 10-35
Among cheats I am gambling; I am the brilliance of the brilliant. I am victory, I am resolve, and I am the goodness of the good.
dyūtaṃ chalayatāmasmi tejastejasvināmaham jayo'smi vyavasāyo'smi sattvaṃ sattvavatāmaham 10-36
Among the Vrishnis I am Vasudeva (Krishna); among the Pandavas, Dhananjaya (Arjuna); among sages I am Vyasa; and among poets, the poet Ushana (Shukracharya).
vṛṣṇīnāṃ vāsudevo'smi pāṇḍavānāṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ munīnāmapyahaṃ vyāsaḥ kavīnāmuśanā kaviḥ 10-37
Among those who punish I am the rod of authority; among those who seek victory, sound policy. Among secrets I am silence, and in the wise I am wisdom.
daṇḍo damayatāmasmi nītirasmi jigīṣatām maunaṃ caivāsmi guhyānāṃ jñānaṃ jñānavatāmaham 10-38
Whatever is the seed of all beings, that too am I, Arjuna. There is no creature, moving or still, that could exist without me.
yaccāpi sarvabhūtānāṃ bījaṃ tadahamarjuna na tadasti vinā yatsyānmayā bhūtaṃ carācaram 10-39
There is no end to my divine glories, Parantapa. What I have said is only a brief indication of their extent.
nānto'sti mama divyānāṃ vibhūtīnāṃ parantapa eṣa tūddeśataḥ prokto vibhūtervistaro mayā 10-40
Whatever being has glory, beauty or great strength, know that it springs from just a fragment of my splendour.
yadyadvibhūtimatsattvaṃ śrīmadūrjitameva vā tattadevāvagaccha tvaṃ mama tejoṃ'śasaṃbhavam 10-41
But what use is all this detail to you, Arjuna? I stand supporting this entire universe with a single fraction of myself.
athavā bahunaitena kiṃ jñātena tavārjuna viṣṭabhyāhamidaṃ kṛtsnamekāṃśena sthito jagat 10-42
Out of kindness to me you have spoken this supreme secret teaching about the Self, and by your words this confusion of mine is gone.
arjuna uvāca madanugrahāya paramaṃ guhyamadhyātmasaṃjñitam yattvayoktaṃ vacastena moho'yaṃ vigato mama 11-1
I have heard from you at length about how beings arise and pass away, lotus-eyed one, and also about your imperishable greatness.
bhavāpyayau hi bhūtānāṃ śrutau vistaraśo mayā tvattaḥ kamalapatrākṣa māhātmyamapi cāvyayam 11-2
It is just as you have described yourself, Supreme Lord. Yet I long to see your divine, sovereign form, Supreme Person.
evametadyathāttha tvamātmānaṃ parameśvara draṣṭumicchāmi te rūpamaiśvaraṃ puruṣottama 11-3
If you think it is possible for me to see it, Lord, then, master of yoga, show me your imperishable Self.
manyase yadi tacchakyaṃ mayā draṣṭumiti prabho yogeśvara tato me tvaṃ darśayātmānamavyayam 11-4
Behold, Partha, my forms by the hundreds and thousands, of many kinds, divine, of many colours and shapes.
paśya me pārtha rūpāṇi śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ nānāvidhāni divyāni nānāvarṇākṛtīni ca 11-5
Behold the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Ashvins and the Maruts as well. Behold many wonders never seen before, Bharata.
paśyādityānvasūnrudrānaśvinau marutastathā bahūnyadṛṣṭapūrvāṇi paśyāścaryāṇi bhārata 11-6
Here, today, Gudakesha, see the whole universe, moving and still, gathered in one place within my body, and whatever else you wish to see.
ihaikasthaṃ jagatkṛtsnaṃ paśyādya sacarācaram mama dehe guḍākeśa yaccānyad draṣṭumicchasi 11-7
But you cannot see me with these eyes of yours. I give you divine sight: behold my sovereign power.
na tu māṃ śakyase draṣṭumanenaiva svacakṣuṣā divyaṃ dadāmi te cakṣuḥ paśya me yogamaiśvaram 11-8
Having spoken thus, O King, Hari, the great lord of yoga, then revealed to Partha his supreme, sovereign form.
sañjaya uvāca evamuktvā tato rājanmahāyogeśvaro hariḥ darśayāmāsa pārthāya paramaṃ rūpamaiśvaram 11-9
It had countless mouths and eyes and countless wondrous sights, countless divine ornaments, and countless divine weapons held aloft.
anekavaktranayanamanekādbhutadarśanam anekadivyābharaṇaṃ divyānekodyatāyudham 11-10
He wore divine garlands and garments and was anointed with divine fragrances. That god was all wonder, boundless, with faces turned in every direction.
divyamālyāmbaradharaṃ divyagandhānulepanam sarvāścaryamayaṃ devamanantaṃ viśvatomukham 11-11
If the light of a thousand suns were to blaze up in the sky all at once, that might resemble the radiance of that great being.
divi sūryasahasrasya bhavedyugapadutthitā yadi bhāḥ sadṛśī sā syādbhāsastasya mahātmanaḥ 11-12
There, in the body of the god of gods, the Pandava then saw the entire universe, divided in many ways, gathered together in one place.
tatraikasthaṃ jagatkṛtsnaṃ pravibhaktamanekadhā apaśyaddevadevasya śarīre pāṇḍavastadā 11-13

It is outside and inside all beings, unmoving and also moving; being so subtle, it cannot be grasped; it is far away and also near.
bahirantaśca bhūtānāmacaraṃ carameva ca sūkṣmatvāttadavijñeyaṃ dūrasthaṃ cāntike ca tat 13-15
Undivided, it yet seems to stand divided among beings. It is to be known as the sustainer of beings, the one who devours them and the one who brings them forth.
avibhaktaṃ ca bhūteṣu vibhaktamiva ca sthitam bhūtabhartṛ ca tajjñeyaṃ grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca 13-16
It is the light of all lights, said to lie beyond darkness. It is knowledge, the thing to be known, and what knowledge leads to, seated in the heart of everyone.
jyotiṣāmapi tajjyotistamasaḥ paramucyate jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānagamyaṃ hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam 13-17
So the field, knowledge and what is to be known have been described in brief. My devotee, understanding this, becomes fit to attain my state of being.
iti kṣetraṃ tathā jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ coktaṃ samāsataḥ madbhakta etadvijñāya madbhāvāyopapadyate 13-18
Know that Prakriti and Purusha are both without beginning, and know that the changes of form and the gunas arise from Prakriti.
prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva viddhyanādī ubhāvapi vikārāṃśca guṇāṃścaiva viddhi prakṛtisaṃbhavān 13-19
Prakriti is said to be the cause behind effect, instrument and agency; Purusha is said to be the cause behind the experiencing of pleasure and pain.
kāryakaraṇakartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtirucyate puruṣaḥ sukhaduḥkhānāṃ bhoktṛtve heturucyate 13-20
Dwelling in Prakriti, Purusha experiences the gunas born of Prakriti; its attachment to the gunas is the cause of its births in good and evil wombs.
puruṣaḥ prakṛtistho hi bhuṅkte prakṛtijānguṇān kāraṇaṃ guṇasaṅgo'sya sadasadyonijanmasu 13-21
The supreme Purusha in this body is also called the witness, the one who consents, the sustainer, the experiencer, the great Lord and the supreme Self.
upadraṣṭānumantā ca bhartā bhoktā maheśvaraḥ paramātmeti cāpyukto dehe'sminpuruṣaḥ paraḥ 13-22
One who knows Purusha and Prakriti together with the gunas in this way is not born again, however he may be living.
ya evaṃ vetti puruṣaṃ prakṛtiṃ ca guṇaiḥ saha sarvathā vartamāno'pi na sa bhūyo'bhijāyate 13-23
Some see the Self within themselves by their own self through meditation; others by the path of Sankhya; and still others by the yoga of action.
dhyānenātmani paśyanti kecidātmānamātmanā anye sāṃkhyena yogena karmayogena cāpare 13-24
Still others, not knowing this themselves, worship after hearing it from others; they too, devoted to what they have heard, cross beyond death.
anye tvevamajānantaḥ śrutvānyebhya upāsate te'pi cātitarantyeva mṛtyuṃ śrutiparāyaṇāḥ 13-25
Whatever being comes into existence, still or moving, know, best of the Bharatas, that it arises from the union of the field and the knower of the field.
yāvatsaṃjāyate kiṃcitsattvaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam kṣetrakṣetrajñasaṃyogāttadviddhi bharatarṣabha 13-26
One who sees the supreme Lord abiding equally in all beings, the imperishable within the perishing — that person truly sees.
samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhantaṃ parameśvaram vinaśyatsvavinaśyantaṃ yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati 13-27
Seeing the Lord present equally everywhere, he does not harm the Self by the self, and so he reaches the highest goal.
samaṃ paśyanhi sarvatra samavasthitamīśvaram na hinastyātmanātmānaṃ tato yāti parāṃ gatim 13-28
One who sees that all actions are carried out entirely by Prakriti alone, and that the Self is not the doer, truly sees.
prakṛtyaiva ca karmāṇi kriyamāṇāni sarvaśaḥ yaḥ paśyati tathātmānamakartāraṃ sa paśyati 13-29
When one perceives the separate existence of beings as resting in the One, and their spreading out as coming from that alone, one then attains Brahman.
yadā bhūtapṛthagbhāvamekasthamanupaśyati tata eva ca vistāraṃ brahma saṃpadyate tadā 13-30
Being without beginning and beyond the gunas, this imperishable supreme Self, Kaunteya, though dwelling in the body, neither acts nor is tainted.
anāditvānnirguṇatvātparamātmāyamavyayaḥ śarīrastho'pi kaunteya na karoti na lipyate 13-31
Just as all-pervading space is not tainted because of its subtlety, so the Self, present throughout the body, is not tainted.
yathā sarvagataṃ saukṣmyādākāśaṃ nopalipyate sarvatrāvasthito dehe tathātmā nopalipyate 13-32
Just as the one sun lights up this whole world, so the owner of the field lights up the whole field, Bharata.
yathā prakāśayatyekaḥ kṛtsnaṃ lokamimaṃ raviḥ kṣetraṃ kṣetrī tathā kṛtsnaṃ prakāśayati bhārata 13-33
Those who see with the eye of knowledge the difference between the field and its knower, and how beings are freed from Prakriti, reach the Supreme.
kṣetrakṣetrajñayorevamantaraṃ jñānacakṣuṣā bhūtaprakṛtimokṣaṃ ca ye viduryānti te param 13-34
I will again set out the supreme knowledge, the finest of all knowledge, by knowing which all the sages passed from this world to the highest perfection.
paraṃ bhūyaḥ pravakṣyāmi jñānānāṃ jñānamuttamam yajjñātvā munayaḥ sarve parāṃ siddhimito gatāḥ 14-1
Those who take refuge in this knowledge come to share my nature; they are not born even at the creation of the world, nor shaken at its dissolution.
idaṃ jñānamupāśritya mama sādharmyamāgatāḥ sarge'pi nopajāyante pralaye na vyathanti ca 14-2
My womb is the great Brahman — primal Prakriti — and in it I place the seed; from that, Bharata, all beings come into being.
mama yonirmahadbrahma tasmingarbhaṃ dadhāmyaham saṃbhavaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tato bhavati bhārata 14-3
Whatever forms are born in any womb, Kaunteya, the great Brahman is their womb, and I am the father who gives the seed.
sarvayoniṣu kaunteya mūrtayaḥ saṃbhavanti yāḥ tāsāṃ brahma mahadyonirahaṃ bījapradaḥ pitā 14-4
Sattva, rajas and tamas — these gunas born of Prakriti bind the imperishable embodied self to the body, mighty-armed one.
sattvaṃ rajastama iti guṇāḥ prakṛtisaṃbhavāḥ nibadhnanti mahābāho dehe dehinamavyayam 14-5
Of these, sattva, being pure, is illuminating and free from affliction; yet it binds through attachment to happiness and attachment to knowledge, sinless one.
tatra sattvaṃ nirmalatvātprakāśakamanāmayam sukhasaṅgena badhnāti jñānasaṅgena cānagha 14-6
Know rajas to be of the nature of passion, springing from craving and attachment; it binds the embodied self, Kaunteya, through attachment to action.
rajo rāgātmakaṃ viddhi tṛṣṇāsaṅgasamudbhavam tannibadhnāti kaunteya karmasaṅgena dehinam 14-7
Know tamas to be born of ignorance, deluding all embodied beings; it binds them, Bharata, through carelessness, sloth and sleep.
tamastvajñānajaṃ viddhi mohanaṃ sarvadehinām pramādālasyanidrābhistannibadhnāti bhārata 14-8
Sattva attaches one to happiness and rajas to action, Bharata; but tamas, veiling knowledge, attaches one to carelessness.
sattvaṃ sukhe saṃjayati rajaḥ karmaṇi bhārata jñānamāvṛtya tu tamaḥ pramāde saṃjayatyuta 14-9
Sattva prevails by overpowering rajas and tamas, Bharata; rajas prevails by overpowering sattva and tamas; and tamas likewise by overpowering sattva and rajas.
rajastamaścābhibhūya sattvaṃ bhavati bhārata rajaḥ sattvaṃ tamaścaiva tamaḥ sattvaṃ rajastathā 14-10
When the light of knowledge shines through every gateway of this body, then one should know that sattva has grown strong.
sarvadvāreṣu dehe'sminprakāśa upajāyate jñānaṃ yadā tadā vidyādvivṛddhaṃ sattvamityuta 14-11
Greed, busy activity, the launching of ventures, restlessness and longing — these arise when rajas has grown strong, best of the Bharatas.
lobhaḥ pravṛttirārambhaḥ karmaṇāmaśamaḥ spṛhā rajasyetāni jāyante vivṛddhe bharatarṣabha 14-12
Darkness of mind, inertia, carelessness and delusion — these arise when tamas has grown strong, joy of the Kurus.
aprakāśo'pravṛttiśca pramādo moha eva ca tamasyetāni jāyante vivṛddhe kurunandana 14-13
If the embodied one meets death when sattva is dominant, he goes to the pure worlds of those who know the highest.
yadā sattve pravṛddhe tu pralayaṃ yāti dehabhṛt tadottamavidāṃ lokānamalānpratipadyate 14-14
Dying in rajas, one is born among those attached to action; dying in tamas, one is born in deluded wombs.
rajasi pralayaṃ gatvā karmasaṅgiṣu jāyate tathā pralīnastamasi mūḍhayoniṣu jāyate 14-15
The fruit of good action, it is said, is sattvic and pure; the fruit of rajas is pain, and the fruit of tamas is ignorance.
karmaṇaḥ sukṛtasyāhuḥ sāttvikaṃ nirmalaṃ phalam rajasastu phalaṃ duḥkhamajñānaṃ tamasaḥ phalam 14-16
From sattva comes knowledge, and from rajas greed; from tamas come carelessness and delusion, and ignorance as well.
sattvātsaṃjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca pramādamohau tamaso bhavato'jñānameva ca 14-17
Those established in sattva rise upward; the rajasic stay in the middle; the tamasic, sunk in the lowest of the gunas, go downward.
ūrdhvaṃ gacchanti sattvasthā madhye tiṣṭhanti rājasāḥ jaghanyaguṇavṛttisthā adho gacchanti tāmasāḥ 14-18
When the seer perceives no doer other than the gunas, and knows what lies beyond the gunas, he attains my state of being.
nānyaṃ guṇebhyaḥ kartāraṃ yadā draṣṭānupaśyati guṇebhyaśca paraṃ vetti madbhāvaṃ so'dhigacchati 14-19
Going beyond these three gunas from which the body arises, the embodied one is freed from the sorrows of birth, death and old age, and tastes immortality.
guṇānetānatītya trīndehī dehasamudbhavān janmamṛtyujarāduḥkhairvimukto'mṛtamaśnute 14-20
By what marks is one known who has gone beyond these three gunas, Lord? How does such a person behave, and how does one pass beyond these three gunas?
arjuna uvāca kairliṅgaistrīnguṇānetānatīto bhavati prabho kimācāraḥ kathaṃ caitāṃstrīnguṇānativartate 14-21
Pandava, one who does not resent illumination, activity or delusion when they arise, nor long for them when they subside…
prakāśaṃ ca pravṛttiṃ ca mohameva ca pāṇḍava na dveṣṭi saṃpravṛttāni na nivṛttāni kāṅkṣati 14-22
…who sits as if indifferent, unshaken by the gunas, who stays steady knowing simply that it is the gunas that are at work, and does not waver…
udāsīnavadāsīno guṇairyo na vicālyate guṇā vartanta ityeva yo'vatiṣṭhati neṅgate 14-23
…who is the same in pain and pleasure, rests in the self, regards a clod, a stone and gold alike, treats the pleasant and unpleasant equally, is steady, and takes blame and praise of himself alike…
samaduḥkhasukhaḥ svasthaḥ samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ tulyapriyāpriyo dhīrastulyanindātmasaṃstutiḥ 14-24
…who is the same in honour and dishonour, the same toward friend and foe, and has given up every self-driven undertaking — such a one is said to have gone beyond the gunas.
mānāpamānayostulyastulyo mitrāripakṣayoḥ sarvārambhaparityāgī guṇātītaḥ sa ucyate 14-25
And one who serves me with the yoga of unwavering devotion goes beyond these gunas and becomes fit to become Brahman.
māṃ ca yo'vyabhicāreṇa bhaktiyogena sevate sa guṇānsamatītyaitānbrahmabhūyāya kalpate 14-26
For I am the foundation of Brahman — of the immortal and imperishable, of eternal dharma, and of absolute bliss.
brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭhāhamamṛtasyāvyayasya ca śāśvatasya ca dharmasya sukhasyaikāntikasya ca 14-27

They speak of an imperishable ashvattha (sacred fig) tree whose roots point upward and whose branches spread downward. Its leaves are the Vedic hymns, and whoever understands this tree truly knows the Veda.
ūrdhvamūlamadhaḥśākhamaśvatthaṃ prāhuravyayam chandāṃsi yasya parṇāni yastaṃ veda sa vedavit 15-1

Its branches reach both downward and upward, fed and swelled by the gunas, with sense-objects as their young shoots. Below, in the world of humans, its roots stretch on and on, binding people through their actions.
adhaścordhvaṃ prasṛtāstasya śākhā guṇapravṛddhā viṣayapravālāḥ adhaśca mūlānyanusaṃtatāni karmānubandhīni manuṣyaloke 15-2
Its true form cannot be grasped here, nor its end, nor its beginning, nor what it rests on. Cutting down this firmly rooted ashvattha with the strong axe of non-attachment…
na rūpamasyeha tathopalabhyate nānto na cādirna ca saṃpratiṣṭhā aśvatthamenaṃ suvirūḍhamūla- masaṅgaśastreṇa dṛḍhena chittvā 15-3
…one should then seek out that state from which those who reach it never return, thinking: 'I take refuge in that primal Person from whom this ancient flow of creation has streamed forth.'
tataḥ padaṃ tatparimārgitavyaṃ yasmingatā na nivartanti bhūyaḥ tameva cādyaṃ puruṣaṃ prapadye yataḥ pravṛttiḥ prasṛtā purāṇī 15-4

Free of pride and delusion, having overcome the flaw of attachment, always rooted in the Self, with desires fallen away and released from the pairs of opposites called pleasure and pain, the undeluded reach that undying state.
nirmānamohā jitasaṅgadoṣā adhyātmanityā vinivṛttakāmāḥ dvandvairvimuktāḥ sukhaduḥkhasaṃjñai- rgacchantyamūḍhāḥ padamavyayaṃ tat 15-5
Neither the sun nor the moon nor fire lights up that place. Those who go there do not come back; that is my supreme abode.
na tadbhāsayate sūryo na śaśāṅko na pāvakaḥ yadgatvā na nivartante taddhāma paramaṃ mama 15-6
A part of my very own self, eternal, becomes the living soul in this world of living beings; it draws around itself the mind and the five senses, which belong to Prakriti.
mamaivāṃśo jīvaloke jīvabhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ manaḥṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi prakṛtisthāni karṣati 15-7
Whenever this lord of the body takes up a body or leaves one, it carries these along with it, the way the wind carries scents away from their source.
śarīraṃ yadavāpnoti yaccāpyutkrāmatīśvaraḥ gṛhītvaitāni saṃyāti vāyurgandhānivāśayāt 15-8
Presiding over hearing, sight, touch, taste and smell, and over the mind as well, it enjoys the objects of the senses.
śrotraṃ cakṣuḥ sparśanaṃ ca rasanaṃ ghrāṇameva ca adhiṣṭhāya manaścāyaṃ viṣayānupasevate 15-9
Whether it is leaving the body, staying in it, or enjoying experiences while joined with the gunas, the deluded do not perceive it; those with the eye of knowledge do.
utkrāmantaṃ sthitaṃ vāpi bhuñjānaṃ vā guṇānvitam vimūḍhā nānupaśyanti paśyanti jñānacakṣuṣaḥ 15-10
Yogis who strive see it dwelling within themselves. But those whose minds are unrefined and lack understanding do not see it, even when they make the effort.
yatanto yoginaścainaṃ paśyantyātmanyavasthitam yatanto'pyakṛtātmāno nainaṃ paśyantyacetasaḥ 15-11
The radiance in the sun that lights up the whole world, the radiance in the moon and in fire, know that radiance to be mine.
yadādityagataṃ tejo jagadbhāsayate'khilam yaccandramasi yaccāgnau tattejo viddhi māmakam 15-12
Entering the earth, I hold up all beings by my power. Becoming Soma, the essence of sap, I nourish every plant.
gāmāviśya ca bhūtāni dhārayāmyahamojasā puṣṇāmi cauṣadhīḥ sarvāḥ somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ 15-13
Becoming the digestive fire Vaishvanara, I live in the bodies of living beings and, joined with the inward and outward breaths, I digest the four kinds of food.
ahaṃ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṃ dehamāśritaḥ prāṇāpānasamāyuktaḥ pacāmyannaṃ caturvidham 15-14
I am seated in the heart of everyone; from me come memory, knowledge and their loss. I alone am what all the Vedas seek to make known; I am the author of Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas.
sarvasya cāhaṃ hṛdi saṃniviṣṭo mattaḥ smṛtirjñānamapohanaṃ ca vedaiśca sarvairahameva vedyo vedāntakṛdvedavideva cāham 15-15
There are two kinds of persons in this world, the perishable and the imperishable. All beings are the perishable; the unchanging one, standing firm at the core, is called the imperishable.
dvāvimau puruṣau loke kṣaraścākṣara eva ca kṣaraḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭastho'kṣara ucyate 15-16
But there is another, the highest Person, called the Supreme Self, the unchanging Lord who pervades the three worlds and sustains them.
uttamaḥ puruṣastvanyaḥ paramātmetyudāhṛtaḥ yo lokatrayamāviśya bibhartyavyaya īśvaraḥ 15-17
Because I am beyond the perishable and higher even than the imperishable, I am celebrated in the world and in the Veda as Purushottama, the Supreme Person.
yasmātkṣaramatīto'hamakṣarādapi cottamaḥ ato'smi loke vede ca prathitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ 15-18
Whoever, free of confusion, knows me in this way as the Supreme Person knows everything, Bharata, and worships me with their whole being.
yo māmevamasaṃmūḍho jānāti puruṣottamam sa sarvavidbhajati māṃ sarvabhāvena bhārata 15-19
Sinless one, I have now told you this most secret teaching. Understanding it, Bharata, a person becomes truly wise and has done all that needs to be done.
iti guhyatamaṃ śāstramidamuktaṃ mayānagha etadbuddhvā buddhimānsyātkṛtakṛtyaśca bhārata 15-20
Fearlessness, a purified inner being, steadiness in the path of knowledge, generosity, self-restraint, sacrifice, study of scripture, austerity and straightforwardness…
abhayaṃ sattvasaṃśuddhirjñānayogavyavasthitiḥ dānaṃ damaśca yajñaśca svādhyāyastapa ārjavam 16-1
…non-violence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, renunciation, calm, not slandering others, compassion for all beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, a sense of shame and steadiness of purpose…
ahiṃsā satyamakrodhastyāgaḥ śāntirapaiśunam dayā bhūteṣvaloluptvaṃ mārdavaṃ hrīracāpalam 16-2
…vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, freedom from malice and from excessive pride. These, Bharata, belong to one born with the divine nature.
tejaḥ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ śaucamadroho nātimānitā bhavanti saṃpadaṃ daivīmabhijātasya bhārata 16-3
Hypocrisy, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness and ignorance, Partha, belong to one born with the demonic nature.
dambho darpo'bhimānaśca krodhaḥ pāruṣyameva ca ajñānaṃ cābhijātasya pārtha saṃpadamāsurīm 16-4
The divine nature is held to lead to liberation, and the demonic to bondage. Do not grieve, Pandava; you were born with the divine nature.
daivī saṃpadvimokṣāya nibandhāyāsurī matā mā śucaḥ saṃpadaṃ daivīmabhijāto'si pāṇḍava 16-5
There are two kinds of beings created in this world: the divine and the demonic. The divine has been described at length; now, Partha, hear from me about the demonic.
dvau bhūtasargau loke'smindaiva āsura eva ca daivo vistaraśaḥ prokta āsuraṃ pārtha me śṛṇu 16-6
People of demonic nature do not understand what to take up and what to turn away from. Neither purity, nor right conduct, nor truthfulness is found in them.
pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca janā na vidurāsurāḥ na śaucaṃ nāpi cācāro na satyaṃ teṣu vidyate 16-7
They say the world is without truth, without foundation and without God; that it has come about through the union of male and female and nothing else, with desire as its only cause.
asatyamapratiṣṭhaṃ te jagadāhuranīśvaram aparasparasaṃbhūtaṃ kimanyatkāmahaitukam 16-8
Clinging to this view, these lost souls of small understanding and cruel deeds rise up as enemies of the world, bent on its destruction.
etāṃ dṛṣṭimavaṣṭabhya naṣṭātmāno'lpabuddhayaḥ prabhavantyugrakarmāṇaḥ kṣayāya jagato'hitāḥ 16-9
Giving themselves to desire that can never be filled, full of hypocrisy, pride and intoxication, they seize false notions out of delusion and pursue their aims with impure resolves.
kāmamāśritya duṣpūraṃ dambhamānamadānvitāḥ mohādgṛhītvāsadgrāhānpravartante'śucivratāḥ 16-10
Weighed down by endless worries that last until death, treating the enjoyment of desires as the highest goal and convinced that this is all there is…
cintāmaparimeyāṃ ca pralayāntāmupāśritāḥ kāmopabhogaparamā etāvaditi niścitāḥ 16-11
…bound by hundreds of ropes of hope, given over to lust and anger, they strive to pile up wealth by unjust means for the sake of enjoying their desires.
āśāpāśaśatairbaddhāḥ kāmakrodhaparāyaṇāḥ īhante kāmabhogārthamanyāyenārthasañcayān 16-12
'This I have gained today; that wish I will fulfil next. This wealth is mine, and more will be mine again.'
idamadya mayā labdhamimaṃ prāpsye manoratham idamastīdamapi me bhaviṣyati punardhanam 16-13
'That enemy I have killed, and I will kill the others too. I am the master, I am the enjoyer; I am successful, strong and happy.'
asau mayā hataḥ śatrurhaniṣye cāparānapi īśvaro'hamahaṃ bhogī siddho'haṃ balavānsukhī 16-14
'I am rich and well born; who else is my equal? I will perform sacrifices, I will give gifts, I will enjoy myself.' So they speak, led astray by ignorance.
āḍhyo'bhijanavānasmi ko'nyo'sti sadṛśo mayā yakṣye dāsyāmi modiṣya ityajñānavimohitāḥ 16-15
Confused by countless thoughts, caught in a net of delusion and addicted to the enjoyment of desires, they fall into a foul hell.
anekacittavibhrāntā mohajālasamāvṛtāḥ prasaktāḥ kāmabhogeṣu patanti narake'śucau 16-16
Self-admiring, stubborn, drunk on wealth and status, they perform sacrifices in name only, out of show and without following the prescribed rules.
ātmasaṃbhāvitāḥ stabdhā dhanamānamadānvitāḥ yajante nāmayajñaiste dambhenāvidhipūrvakam 16-17
Clinging to ego, force, arrogance, lust and anger, these envious people hate me, who dwell in their own bodies and in the bodies of others.
ahaṃkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca saṃśritāḥ māmātmaparadeheṣu pradviṣanto'bhyasūyakāḥ 16-18
These hateful, cruel, inauspicious people, the lowest of humans, I hurl again and again into demonic wombs within the cycles of birth and death.
tānahaṃ dviṣataḥ krūrānsaṃsāreṣu narādhamān kṣipāmyajasramaśubhānāsurīṣveva yoniṣu 16-19
Having entered demonic wombs, deluded birth after birth, Kaunteya, they never reach me and sink from there to an even lower state.
āsurīṃ yonimāpannā mūḍhā janmani janmani māmaprāpyaiva kaunteya tato yāntyadhamāṃ gatim 16-20
Lust, anger and greed: this is the threefold gate of hell that ruins the self. Therefore one should give up all three.
trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet 16-21
A person released from these three gates of darkness, Kaunteya, does what is truly good for the self, and so reaches the highest goal.
etairvimuktaḥ kaunteya tamodvāraistribhirnaraḥ ācaratyātmanaḥ śreyastato yāti parāṃ gatim 16-22
One who sets aside the guidance of scripture and acts on the impulse of desire attains neither perfection, nor happiness, nor the highest goal.
yaḥ śāstravidhimutsṛjya vartate kāmakārataḥ na sa siddhimavāpnoti na sukhaṃ na parāṃ gatim 16-23
So let scripture be your authority in deciding what should and should not be done. Knowing what the scriptural injunctions say, you should do your work here.
tasmācchāstraṃ pramāṇaṃ te kāryākāryavyavasthitau jñātvā śāstravidhānoktaṃ karma kartumihārhasi 16-24
Krishna, what about those who set aside the rules of scripture yet worship with faith? What is their standing: sattva, rajas or tamas?
arjuna uvāca ye śāstravidhimutsṛjya yajante śraddhayānvitāḥ teṣāṃ niṣṭhā tu kā kṛṣṇa sattvamāho rajastamaḥ 17-1
The faith of embodied beings is of three kinds, born of each one's own nature: sattvic, rajasic and tamasic. Hear about it.
trividhā bhavati śraddhā dehināṃ sā svabhāvajā sāttvikī rājasī caiva tāmasī ceti tāṃ śṛṇu 17-2
Everyone's faith takes the shape of their inner nature, Bharata. A person is made of faith: whatever one's faith is, that is what one is.
sattvānurūpā sarvasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata śraddhāmayo'yaṃ puruṣo yo yacchraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ 17-3
Sattvic people worship the gods; rajasic people worship yakshas and rakshasas; and tamasic people worship ghosts and hosts of spirits.
yajante sāttvikā devānyakṣarakṣāṃsi rājasāḥ pretānbhūtagaṇāṃścānye yajante tāmasā janāḥ 17-4
Those people who undergo harsh austerities not sanctioned by scripture, driven by hypocrisy and ego, and carried along by the force of desire and attachment…
aśāstravihitaṃ ghoraṃ tapyante ye tapo janāḥ dambhāhaṃkārasaṃyuktāḥ kāmarāgabalānvitāḥ 17-5
…senselessly tormenting the elements that make up the body, and me as well, who dwell within the body: know them to be of demonic resolve.
karṣayantaḥ śarīrasthaṃ bhūtagrāmamacetasaḥ māṃ caivāntaḥśarīrasthaṃ tānviddhyāsuraniścayān 17-6
Even the food each person likes is of three kinds, and so are sacrifice, austerity and charity. Hear how they differ.
āhārastvapi sarvasya trividho bhavati priyaḥ yajñastapastathā dānaṃ teṣāṃ bhedamimaṃ śṛṇu 17-7
Foods that increase life, vitality, strength, health, happiness and contentment, and that are tasty, rich, substantial and pleasing to the heart, are dear to sattvic people.
āyuḥsattvabalārogyasukhaprītivivardhanāḥ rasyāḥ snigdhāḥ sthirā hṛdyā āhārāḥ sāttvikapriyāḥ 17-8
Foods that are bitter, sour, salty, overly hot, pungent, dry and burning are favoured by rajasic people; they bring pain, grief and illness.
kaṭvamlalavaṇātyuṣṇatīkṣṇarūkṣavidāhinaḥ āhārā rājasasyeṣṭā duḥkhaśokāmayapradāḥ 17-9
Food that is stale, tasteless, putrid, kept overnight, left over by others, or impure is dear to tamasic people.
yātayāmaṃ gatarasaṃ pūti paryuṣitaṃ ca yat ucchiṣṭamapi cāmedhyaṃ bhojanaṃ tāmasapriyam 17-10
Sacrifice offered according to scriptural rule by those who seek no reward, with the mind settled on the thought that it simply ought to be done, is sattvic.
aphalākāṅkṣibhiryajño vidhidṛṣṭo ya ijyate yaṣṭavyameveti manaḥ samādhāya sa sāttvikaḥ 17-11
But sacrifice performed with an eye on the reward, or merely for show, know that to be rajasic, best of the Bharatas.
abhisaṃdhāya tu phalaṃ dambhārthamapi caiva yat ijyate bharataśreṣṭha taṃ yajñaṃ viddhi rājasam 17-12
Sacrifice that ignores the rules, distributes no food, lacks mantras, gives no fee to the priests and is devoid of faith is called tamasic.
vidhihīnamasṛṣṭānnaṃ mantrahīnamadakṣiṇam śraddhāvirahitaṃ yajñaṃ tāmasaṃ paricakṣate 17-13
Honouring the gods, the twice-born, teachers and the wise; purity, straightforwardness, celibacy and non-violence: this is called austerity of the body.
devadvijaguruprājñapūjanaṃ śaucamārjavam brahmacaryamahiṃsā ca śārīraṃ tapa ucyate 17-14
Speech that causes no distress, that is true, pleasant and beneficial, together with regular recitation of scripture: this is called austerity of speech.
anudvegakaraṃ vākyaṃ satyaṃ priyahitaṃ ca yat svādhyāyābhyasanaṃ caiva vāṅmayaṃ tapa ucyate 17-15
Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-control and purity of feeling: this is called austerity of the mind.
manaḥ prasādaḥ saumyatvaṃ maunamātmavinigrahaḥ bhāvasaṃśuddhirityetattapo mānasamucyate 17-16
When this threefold austerity is practised with the highest faith by disciplined people who seek no reward, it is called sattvic.
śraddhayā parayā taptaṃ tapastattrividhaṃ naraiḥ aphalākāṅkṣibhiryuktaiḥ sāttvikaṃ paricakṣate 17-17
Austerity performed to gain respect, honour and reverence, and done with hypocrisy, is called rajasic here; it is unsteady and does not last.
satkāramānapūjārthaṃ tapo dambhena caiva yat kriyate tadiha proktaṃ rājasaṃ calamadhruvam 17-18
Austerity undertaken out of a foolish obstinacy, through torment of oneself, or in order to ruin another, is declared tamasic.
mūḍhagrāheṇātmano yatpīḍayā kriyate tapaḥ parasyotsādanārthaṃ vā tattāmasamudāhṛtam 17-19
A gift given simply because giving is right, to someone who can do nothing in return, at the proper place and time and to a worthy recipient, is held to be sattvic.
dātavyamiti yaddānaṃ dīyate'nupakāriṇe deśe kāle ca pātre ca taddānaṃ sāttvikaṃ smṛtam 17-20
But a gift given to get something back, or with a reward in view, or given grudgingly, is held to be rajasic.
yattu pratyupakārārthaṃ phalamuddiśya vā punaḥ dīyate ca parikliṣṭaṃ taddānaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam 17-21
A gift given at the wrong place and time, to unworthy people, without respect and with contempt, is declared tamasic.
adeśakāle yaddānamapātrebhyaśca dīyate asatkṛtamavajñātaṃ tattāmasamudāhṛtam 17-22
'Om Tat Sat' is remembered as the threefold designation of Brahman. By it, in ancient times, the brahmins, the Vedas and the sacrifices were ordained.
oṃtatsaditi nirdeśo brahmaṇastrividhaḥ smṛtaḥ brāhmaṇāstena vedāśca yajñāśca vihitāḥ purā 17-23
That is why those who speak of Brahman always begin their acts of sacrifice, charity and austerity, performed as the scriptures direct, by uttering 'Om'.
tasmādomityudāhṛtya yajñadānatapaḥkriyāḥ pravartante vidhānoktāḥ satataṃ brahmavādinām 17-24
With the word 'Tat', and without aiming at any reward, those who seek liberation perform the various acts of sacrifice, austerity and charity.
tadityanabhisandhāya phalaṃ yajñatapaḥkriyāḥ dānakriyāśca vividhāḥ kriyante mokṣakāṅkṣibhiḥ 17-25
The word 'Sat' is used in the sense of reality and of goodness; likewise, Partha, the word 'Sat' is applied to any praiseworthy act.
sadbhāve sādhubhāve ca sadityetatprayujyate praśaste karmaṇi tathā sacchabdaḥ pārtha yujyate 17-26
Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and charity is also called 'Sat', and any action done for that purpose is likewise named 'Sat'.
yajñe tapasi dāne ca sthitiḥ saditi cocyate karma caiva tadarthīyaṃ sadityevābhidhīyate 17-27
Whatever is offered, given, practised as austerity or done without faith is called 'asat', Partha; it is of no value, either after death or here.
aśraddhayā hutaṃ dattaṃ tapastaptaṃ kṛtaṃ ca yat asadityucyate pārtha na ca tatpretya no iha 17-28
Mighty-armed one, Hrishikesha, slayer of the demon Keshi, I want to understand the true nature of renunciation (sannyasa) and of relinquishment (tyaga), each one separately.
arjuna uvāca saṃnyāsasya mahābāho tattvamicchāmi veditum tyāgasya ca hṛṣīkeśa pṛthakkeśiniṣūdana 18-1
The wise understand sannyasa as setting aside actions driven by desire, while the discerning describe tyaga as giving up the fruits of every action.
kāmyānāṃ karmaṇāṃ nyāsaṃ saṃnyāsaṃ kavayo viduḥ sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṃ prāhustyāgaṃ vicakṣaṇāḥ 18-2
Some thinkers hold that action itself should be abandoned because it is tainted with fault; others say that acts of sacrifice, giving and austerity must never be abandoned.
tyājyaṃ doṣavadityeke karma prāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ yajñadānatapaḥkarma na tyājyamiti cāpare 18-3
Now hear my firm conclusion about relinquishment, best of the Bharatas; for relinquishment, tiger among men, is declared to be of three kinds.
niścayaṃ śṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharatasattama tyāgo hi puruṣavyāghra trividhaḥ saṃprakīrtitaḥ 18-4
Acts of sacrifice, giving and austerity should not be given up; they ought to be performed, for sacrifice, giving and austerity purify even the wise.
yajñadānatapaḥkarma na tyājyaṃ kāryameva tat yajño dānaṃ tapaścaiva pāvanāni manīṣiṇām 18-5
Yet even these acts should be done after giving up attachment and the fruits. This, Partha, is my settled and highest view.
etānyapi tu karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalāni ca kartavyānīti me pārtha niścitaṃ matamuttamam 18-6
It is not right to renounce an action that is one's duty. Giving it up out of delusion is called tamasic relinquishment.
niyatasya tu saṃnyāsaḥ karmaṇo nopapadyate mohāttasya parityāgastāmasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ 18-7
Whoever gives up an action because it is painful, or out of fear of bodily hardship, makes a rajasic relinquishment and does not gain the reward of relinquishment.
duḥkhamityeva yatkarma kāyakleśabhayāttyajet sa kṛtvā rājasaṃ tyāgaṃ naiva tyāgaphalaṃ labhet 18-8
When a prescribed action is done simply because it ought to be done, Arjuna, giving up attachment and the fruit, that relinquishment is considered sattvic.
kāryamityeva yatkarma niyataṃ kriyate'rjuna saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalaṃ caiva sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mataḥ 18-9
The relinquisher filled with sattva, wise and free of doubt, neither resents unpleasant work nor clings to pleasant work.
na dveṣṭyakuśalaṃ karma kuśale nānuṣajjate tyāgī sattvasamāviṣṭo medhāvī chinnasaṃśayaḥ 18-10
No embodied being can give up actions completely. But one who gives up the fruits of action is truly called a relinquisher.
na hi dehabhṛtā śakyaṃ tyaktuṃ karmāṇyaśeṣataḥ yastu karmaphalatyāgī sa tyāgītyabhidhīyate 18-11
The fruit of action is threefold after death for those who have not relinquished: unwanted, wanted and mixed. For those who have renounced, there is none at all.
aniṣṭamiṣṭaṃ miśraṃ ca trividhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam bhavatyatyāgināṃ pretya na tu saṃnyāsināṃ kvacit 18-12
Mighty-armed one, learn from me these five causes for the accomplishment of every action, as set out in the Sankhya teaching that brings action to its end.
pañcaitāni mahābāho kāraṇāni nibodha me sāṃkhye kṛtānte proktāni siddhaye sarvakarmaṇām 18-13
They are the seat of action (the body), the doer, the various instruments (the senses), the many distinct kinds of effort, and fifth among them, the divine factor (daiva).
adhiṣṭhānaṃ tathā kartā karaṇaṃ ca pṛthagvidham vividhāśca pṛthakceṣṭā daivaṃ caivātra pañcamam 18-14
Whatever action a person begins with body, speech or mind, whether right or wrong, these five are its causes.
śarīravāṅmanobhiryatkarma prārabhate naraḥ nyāyyaṃ vā viparītaṃ vā pañcaite tasya hetavaḥ 18-15
That being so, whoever, through an untrained understanding, sees the pure Self alone as the doer, that dull-minded person does not see truly.
tatraivaṃ sati kartāramātmānaṃ kevalaṃ tu yaḥ paśyatyakṛtabuddhitvānna sa paśyati durmatiḥ 18-16
One who has no sense of being the doer and whose understanding is not stained, even if he kills these people, does not kill and is not bound.
yasya nāhaṃkṛto bhāvo buddhiryasya na lipyate hatvāpi sa imā~llokānna hanti na nibadhyate 18-17
Knowledge, the object known and the knower are the threefold impulse to action; the instrument, the act and the doer are the threefold basis of action.
jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ parijñātā trividhā karmacodanā karaṇaṃ karma karteti trividhaḥ karmasaṃgrahaḥ 18-18
Knowledge, action and the doer are each said to be of three kinds, differing according to the gunas, in the analysis of the gunas. Hear about them as they are.
jñānaṃ karma ca kartā ca tridhaiva guṇabhedataḥ procyate guṇasaṃkhyāne yathāvacchṛṇu tānyapi 18-19
The knowledge by which one sees a single imperishable reality in all beings, undivided among the divided, know that knowledge to be sattvic.
sarvabhūteṣu yenaikaṃ bhāvamavyayamīkṣate avibhaktaṃ vibhakteṣu tajjñānaṃ viddhi sāttvikam 18-20
But the knowledge that sees in all beings separate entities of various kinds, each distinct from the others, know that knowledge to be rajasic.
pṛthaktvena tu yajjñānaṃ nānābhāvānpṛthagvidhān vetti sarveṣu bhūteṣu tajjñānaṃ viddhi rājasam 18-21
And the knowledge that clings to one single thing as if it were the whole, without reason, without grasp of the truth, and narrow, is declared tamasic.
yattu kṛtsnavadekasminkārye saktamahaitukam atattvārthavadalpaṃ ca tattāmasamudāhṛtam 18-22
An action that is prescribed, done without attachment, without liking or dislike, by one who does not seek its fruit, is called sattvic.
niyataṃ saṅgarahitamarāgadveṣataḥ kṛtam aphalaprepsunā karma yattatsāttvikamucyate 18-23
But an action done by one craving desires, or with ego, involving a great deal of strain, is called rajasic.
yattu kāmepsunā karma sāhaṃkāreṇa vā punaḥ kriyate bahulāyāsaṃ tadrājasamudāhṛtam 18-24
An action undertaken out of delusion, without regard for its consequences, loss, harm to others, or one's own capacity, is called tamasic.
anubandhaṃ kṣayaṃ hiṃsāmanavekṣya ca pauruṣam mohādārabhyate karma yattattāmasamucyate 18-25
A doer who is free of attachment, does not talk of 'I', is full of steadiness and zeal, and is unmoved by success or failure, is called sattvic.
muktasaṅgo'nahaṃvādī dhṛtyutsāhasamanvitaḥ siddhyasiddhyornirvikāraḥ kartā sāttvika ucyate 18-26
A doer who is driven by passion, eager for the fruits of action, greedy, harmful by nature, impure, and swept by joy and grief, is called rajasic.
rāgī karmaphalaprepsurlubdho hiṃsātmako'śuciḥ harṣaśokānvitaḥ kartā rājasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ 18-27
A doer who is undisciplined, crude, stubborn, deceitful, malicious, lazy, gloomy and given to delay, is called tamasic.
ayuktaḥ prākṛtaḥ stabdhaḥ śaṭho naiṣkṛtiko'lasaḥ viṣādī dīrghasūtrī ca kartā tāmasa ucyate 18-28
Now hear, Dhananjaya, the threefold division of understanding and of resolve according to the gunas, which I will explain fully and one by one.
buddherbhedaṃ dhṛteścaiva guṇatastrividhaṃ śṛṇu procyamānamaśeṣeṇa pṛthaktvena dhanaṃjaya 18-29

The understanding that knows engagement and withdrawal, what should and should not be done, what is to be feared and what is not, and what binds and what frees, that understanding, Partha, is sattvic.
pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca kāryākārye bhayābhaye bandhaṃ mokṣaṃ ca yā vetti buddhiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī 18-30
The understanding by which one judges dharma and adharma, and what should and should not be done, in a distorted way, that understanding, Partha, is rajasic.
yayā dharmamadharmaṃ ca kāryaṃ cākāryameva ca ayathāvatprajānāti buddhiḥ sā pārtha rājasī 18-31
The understanding that, wrapped in darkness, takes adharma for dharma and sees everything upside down, that understanding, Partha, is tamasic.
adharmaṃ dharmamiti yā manyate tamasāvṛtā sarvārthānviparītāṃśca buddhiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī 18-32
The resolve by which one holds steady the workings of the mind, the life-breath and the senses through unwavering yoga, that resolve, Partha, is sattvic.
dhṛtyā yayā dhārayate manaḥprāṇendriyakriyāḥ yogenāvyabhicāriṇyā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī 18-33
But the resolve by which one holds on to dharma, pleasure and wealth, Arjuna, craving their fruits out of attachment, that resolve, Partha, is rajasic.
yayā tu dharmakāmārthāndhṛtyā dhārayate'rjuna prasaṅgena phalākāṅkṣī dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha rājasī 18-34
The resolve by which a dull-witted person refuses to let go of sleep, fear, grief, despondency and arrogance, that resolve, Partha, is tamasic.
yayā svapnaṃ bhayaṃ śokaṃ viṣādaṃ madameva ca na vimuñcati durmedhā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī 18-35
Now hear from me, best of the Bharatas, about the three kinds of happiness: the happiness in which one finds delight through practice and arrives at the end of sorrow…
sukhaṃ tvidānīṃ trividhaṃ śṛṇu me bharatarṣabha abhyāsādramate yatra duḥkhāntaṃ ca nigacchati 18-36
…which is like poison at first but like nectar in the end, born of the clarity of one's own understanding of the Self: that happiness is called sattvic.
yattadagre viṣamiva pariṇāme'mṛtopamam tatsukhaṃ sāttvikaṃ proktamātmabuddhiprasādajam 18-37
The happiness that comes from the contact of the senses with their objects, nectar-like at first but like poison in the end, is remembered as rajasic.
viṣayendriyasaṃyogādyattadagre'mṛtopamam pariṇāme viṣamiva tatsukhaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam 18-38
The happiness that deludes the self both at the beginning and in its outcome, arising from sleep, sloth and carelessness, is declared tamasic.
yadagre cānubandhe ca sukhaṃ mohanamātmanaḥ nidrālasyapramādotthaṃ tattāmasamudāhṛtam 18-39
There is no being on earth, nor among the gods in heaven, that is free of these three gunas born of Prakriti.
na tadasti pṛthivyāṃ vā divi deveṣu vā punaḥ sattvaṃ prakṛtijairmuktaṃ yadebhiḥ syāttribhirguṇaiḥ 18-40
The duties of brahmins, kshatriyas, vaishyas and shudras, scorcher of foes, are divided according to the gunas that arise from their own nature.
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ ca parantapa karmāṇi pravibhaktāni svabhāvaprabhavairguṇaiḥ 18-41
Calm, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forbearance, straightforwardness, knowledge, realised wisdom and faith in the sacred are the natural work of a brahmin.
śamo damastapaḥ śaucaṃ kṣāntirārjavameva ca jñānaṃ vijñānamāstikyaṃ brahmakarma svabhāvajam 18-42
Valour, vigour, steadiness, skill, not fleeing in battle, generosity and the bearing of a leader are the natural work of a kshatriya.
śauryaṃ tejo dhṛtirdākṣyaṃ yuddhe cāpyapalāyanam dānamīśvarabhāvaśca kṣātraṃ karma svabhāvajam 18-43
Farming, tending cattle and trade are the natural work of a vaishya; work that consists of service is the natural work of a shudra.
kṛṣigaurakṣyavāṇijyaṃ vaiśyakarma svabhāvajam paricaryātmakaṃ karma śūdrasyāpi svabhāvajam 18-44
A person devoted to their own work attains perfection. Hear how one who is intent on their own work reaches that perfection.
sve sve karmaṇyabhirataḥ saṃsiddhiṃ labhate naraḥ svakarmanirataḥ siddhiṃ yathā vindati tacchṛṇu 18-45
By worshipping, through his own work, the one from whom all beings come forth and by whom all this is pervaded, a person attains perfection.
yataḥ pravṛttirbhūtānāṃ yena sarvamidaṃ tatam svakarmaṇā tamabhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ 18-46
Better one's own dharma, even done imperfectly, than another's dharma done well. Doing the work set by one's own nature, one incurs no sin.
śreyānsvadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmātsvanuṣṭhitāt svabhāvaniyataṃ karma kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam 18-47
Kaunteya, one should not abandon the work that comes naturally to one, even if it has flaws; for every undertaking is wrapped in flaws, as fire is wrapped in smoke.
sahajaṃ karma kaunteya sadoṣamapi na tyajet sarvārambhā hi doṣeṇa dhūmenāgnirivāvṛtāḥ 18-48
One whose understanding is unattached everywhere, who has mastered himself and is free of craving, attains through renunciation the supreme perfection of freedom from action.
asaktabuddhiḥ sarvatra jitātmā vigataspṛhaḥ naiṣkarmyasiddhiṃ paramāṃ saṃnyāsenādhigacchati 18-49
Learn from me in brief, Kaunteya, how one who has attained that perfection also attains Brahman, the highest culmination of knowledge.
siddhiṃ prāpto yathā brahma tathāpnoti nibodha me samāsenaiva kaunteya niṣṭhā jñānasya yā parā 18-50
Endowed with a purified understanding, firmly restraining himself with resolve, setting aside sound and the other sense objects, and casting off attraction and aversion…
buddhyā viśuddhayā yukto dhṛtyātmānaṃ niyamya ca śabdādīnviṣayāṃstyaktvā rāgadveṣau vyudasya ca 18-51
…living in solitude, eating lightly, with speech, body and mind controlled, always devoted to the yoga of meditation, and taking refuge in dispassion…
viviktasevī laghvāśī yatavākkāyamānasaḥ dhyānayogaparo nityaṃ vairāgyaṃ samupāśritaḥ 18-52
…letting go of ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possessiveness, free of the sense of 'mine' and at peace, such a person is fit to become Brahman.
ahaṃkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ parigraham vimucya nirmamaḥ śānto brahmabhūyāya kalpate 18-53
Having become Brahman, serene in spirit, he neither grieves nor longs. Equal towards all beings, he attains supreme devotion to me.
brahmabhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu madbhaktiṃ labhate parām 18-54
Through devotion he comes to know me in truth, how great I am and who I am. Then, having known me in truth, he enters into me at once.
bhaktyā māmabhijānāti yāvānyaścāsmi tattvataḥ tato māṃ tattvato jñātvā viśate tadanantaram 18-55
